rationale: Tests the defining clinical feature of obstructed labour — failure of descent despite adequate contractions — anchored to the clinical presentation block.
Tests correct use of the partograph action line — a key tool for detecting obstructed labour early — anchored to the diagnosis and partograph block.
Tests the classic triad of signs in uterine rupture — a high-stakes recognition question anchored to the clinical presentation block.
Tests understanding of uterine repair vs hysterectomy decision — a critical management choice anchored to the management block.
Tests understanding of why breech presentation increases risk of cord prolapse — a key mechanism-based question anchored to the pathophysiology block.
Tests knowledge of the term gestation management of uncomplicated frank breech — a common exam and clinical decision point, anchored to the management block.
Tests the critical technical principle of ventouse cup placement — the most consequential single step in vacuum extraction, anchored to the technique block.
Tests understanding of sequential instrument use — a recognised risk factor for neonatal trauma — anchored to the complications block.
Tests the correct angle and technique for mediolateral episiotomy — a critical procedural knowledge point anchored to the episiotomy technique block.
Tests the assistant's role at caesarean section and specifically the importance of fundal pressure — a practical procedural knowledge point anchored to the CS assistant block.
